name: AMOS 3D
author: Voodoo Software / Europress Software

provenance.note: Present on several APD disks with no documentation. AMOS 3D was a commercial add-on sold by Europress, not public-domain material, so its presence here does not imply redistribution rights.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified. The AMOS PD Library on CD (Weird Science, 1994), archive.org item cdrom-amospdcd. The disc's own Documents/Copyrights states Weird Science claims no copyright over the material, that parts are shareware with fees due, and that users should make no assumption that anything on it is public domain. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: The 3D extension: object//scene keywords (Td Load, Td Object, Td Move X, ...) over a vector engine. A commercial product whose manual is in no archive found so far, so nothing here describes the keywords in prose and `3d.lib` is the entire account of what they do. Two 82-entry variants are on the disc; both explain all 53 ids observed in slot 4, so the two cannot be told apart from the corpus. Andrew Burton's AMOS Extensions List (kept at ultimateamiga.com, updated 2007-07-29), compiled from the AMOS-LIST archives 1994-1998, Amiga magazine clippings and coverdisk CDs. records an AMOS Pro build numbered 1.02AP, which is not this one — this is the AMOS 1.3-era 1.0. AN AMOS 1.3 BUILD EXISTS and is deliberately NOT registered: 3d.lib on the AMOS PD CD (APD266/AMOS_System), banner "3D extension I 1.50", sharing 63 of its 64 keyword names AND the same token ids as this table. Identical ids make the two indistinguishable in a program -- a tokenised program records (slot, id) and never a name -- so a second identity could never win an identification and would only blunt this one. Whether the 1.3 build differs in behaviour has not been checked.
